{"parentUuid":"27a3bcab-b222-487b-8230-ecc51663a1b2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"852c5e2c-9582-4744-b0f3-4fd6296fbf54","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UdvGBsWa9xiDzNk4fxF1dX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# MP2 Setup Exercise — Context-Threshold Warning Hook\n2\t\n3\t**Course:** IPHS 400 Frontiers of AI, Kenyon College, Fall 2026 (Jon Chun)\n4\t**Where this goes:** Student manual, Part 1 (setup), right after the template repo is cloned and `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` has run.\n5\t**Time:** 20–30 minutes. **Token cost:** under 3% of a 5-hour window (the scripts cost nothing at runtime; hooks run outside the model).\n6\t**Rubric link:** Factor B, item B6 \"session hygiene\" (3 pts). The judge checks that the hook works and reads `docs/process/compaction-log.md`.\n7\t**Verified against:** Claude Code hooks and status-line docs as of 2026-09-22. Record your own version with `claude --version` in `notes/setup_check.md`.\n8\t\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\t## Why you are building this\n12\t\n13\tPocock's loop runs one ticket per fresh context: `/clear`, then `/implement #N`. Most tickets finish well inside one window. A long ticket does not, and a model working in a very full context forgets the ticket's acceptance criteria and starts to drift from the spec. The course rule is:\n14\t\n15\t- **Short ticket:** `/clear` before it. Nothing else.\n16\t- **Long ticket:** once context passes **50–60%**, `/compact` at the next **green test** (the end of a `/tdd` red-green-refactor cycle), never in the middle of a failing test, and always with a focus note.\n17\t\n18\tYou cannot follow that rule if you cannot see the number. This exercise gives you a live meter and a warning that fires at the right moment.\n19\t\n20\t## How it works\n21\t\n22\t```mermaid\n23\tflowchart LR\n24\t    CC[\"Claude Code session\"] -- \"session JSON on stdin<br/>(every refresh)\" --> SL[\"ctx_statusline.py<br/>prints: [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\"]\n25\t    SL -- \"writes\" --> ST[\".claude/state/ctx_&lt;session&gt;.json<br/>{pct: 47.2}\"]\n26\t    CC -- \"Stop event<br/>(end of every Claude turn)\" --> G[\"ctx_guard.py\"]\n27\t    ST -- \"reads\" --> G\n28\t    G -- \"first time over 50 / 60 / 80%\" --> W[\"⚠ systemMessage shown to YOU\"]\n29\t    CC -- \"PreCompact event\" --> L[\"ctx_compact_log.py\"]\n30\t    L -- \"appends\" --> LOG[\"docs/process/compaction-log.md<br/>(grading evidence)\"]\n31\t```\n32\t\n33\tThree facts from the Claude Code docs make this design work:\n34\t\n35\t1. **The status line already receives the context percentage** as `context_window.used_percentage` on stdin. The status line is the customizable bar under your prompt.\n36\t2. **A `Stop` hook fires every time Claude finishes a turn.** The end of a turn is where a natural boundary (a green test) happens, so that is when the warning should appear.\n37\t3. **A hook's `systemMessage` is shown to the user, not to Claude.** The warning talks to you, and does not pollute Claude's context.\n38\t\n39\tA hook cannot type `/compact` for you. Slash commands are yours. The hook only warns; you decide.\n40\t\n41\tEach herdr pane or terminal tab running Claude has its own `session_id`, so parallel sessions keep separate meters and never trip each other's warnings.\n42\t\n43\t## The four files\n44\t\n45\t| File | Job | Runs when |\n46\t|---|---|---|\n47\t| `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py` | Shows the meter; records the percentage | Every status-line refresh |\n48\t| `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` | Warns at 50 / 60 / 80% | End of every Claude turn (`Stop`) |\n49\t| `.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py` | Logs each compaction and its focus note | Before every compaction (`PreCompact`) |\n50\t| `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` | Proves the logic works | When `/tdd` or `/code-review` runs the suite |\n51\t\n52\t---\n53\t\n54\t## Step 1 — Check Python\n55\t\n56\tIn Ghostty (macOS) or Windows Terminal (WSL2), inside your `iphs400-mp2-cms` folder:\n57\t\n58\t```bash\n59\tpython3 --version\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\t**Expected:** `Python 3.9` or newer (the `uv` setup from the setup manual gives you 3.12).\n63\t**If you see `command not found`:** macOS runs `xcode-select --install`; WSL2 runs `sudo apt install -y python3`. Then retry.\n64\t\n65\t## Step 2 — Open the hook files\n66\t\n67\tThe template already contains all four files. Open the folder in VS Code:\n68\t\n69\t```bash\n70\tcode .\n71\t```\n72\t\n73\tIn the Explorer panel, expand `.claude/hooks/`. You should see `ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, and `ctx_compact_log.py`.\n74\t\n75\t**If `.claude` is not visible:** VS Code hides nothing by default, but macOS Finder hides dot-folders. Use VS Code, or run `ls -la .claude/hooks` in the terminal.\n76\t\n77\t## Step 3 — Read the status-line script\n78\t\n79\tThis file is complete. Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\n80\t\n81\t```python\n82\t#!/usr/bin/env python3\n83\t\"\"\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\n84\t\n85\tClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\n86\tJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\n87\t  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\n88\t  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\n89\t     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\n90\tIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\n91\t\"\"\"\n92\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n93\t\n94\timport json\n95\timport os\n96\timport sys\n97\timport time\n98\tfrom pathlib import Path\n99\t\n100\t\n101\tdef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\n102\t    ws = data.get(\"workspace\") or {}\n103\t    return Path(\n104\t        os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\n105\t        or ws.get(\"project_dir\")\n106\t        or ws.get(\"current_dir\")\n107\t        or os.getcwd()\n108\t    )\n109\t\n110\t\n111\tdef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\n112\t    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\n113\t    return \"▓\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n114\t\n115\t\n116\tdef main() -> None:\n117\t    try:\n118\t        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n119\t    except Exception:\n120\t        print(\"ctx ?\")\n121\t        return\n122\t\n123\t    model = (data.get(\"model\") or {}).get(\"display_name\", \"Claude\")\n124\t    pct = (data.get(\"context_window\") or {}).get(\"used_percentage\")\n125\t    if pct is None:\n126\t        print(f\"[{model}] ctx --\")\n127\t        return\n128\t    pct = float(pct)\n129\t\n130\t    session = data.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n131\t    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n132\t    try:\n133\t        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n134\t        tmp = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\"\n135\t        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\"pct\": pct, \"ts\": time.time()}))\n136\t        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\")  # atomic swap\n137\t    except OSError:\n138\t        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\n139\t\n140\t    flag = \"  ⚠ compact at next green test\" if pct >= 60 else \"\"\n141\t    print(f\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\")\n142\t\n143\t\n144\tif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n145\t    main()\n146\t```\n147\t\n148\t## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\n149\t\n150\tThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Seven of the ten tests in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` fail until you finish it. This is your first practice run of the loop on something tiny.\n151\t\n152\tIn a fresh Claude Code session:\n153\t\n154\t```text\n155\t/clear\n156\t/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\t`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. You do not type `pytest` yourself.\n160\t\n161\tThe rules `decide()` must follow:\n162\t\n163\t- Map the percentage to a band: 0 = below 50, 1 = 50+, 2 = 60+, 3 = 80+ (the thresholds come from `thresholds()`).\n164\t- **Warn once per upward crossing.** Going from 52% to 55% must stay quiet.\n165\t- **Re-arm after compaction.** When usage drops (after `/compact` or `/clear`), remember the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n166\t\n167\tWhen the tests pass, compare your version with the complete file below.\n168\t\n169\t\n170\t## Step 5 — Read the compaction logger\n171\t\n172\tThis file is complete. It writes the evidence the judge reads for rubric item B6.\n173\t\n174\t```python\n175\t#!/usr/bin/env python3\n176\t\"\"\"PreCompact hook: log every compaction to docs/process/compaction-log.md.\n177\t\n178\tThis is grading evidence for rubric item B6 (session hygiene):\n179\t  - trigger \"manual\" + a focus note  = you compacted on purpose (good)\n180\t  - trigger \"auto\"                   = the session overflowed (fix the habit)\n181\tNever exits 2: exit 2 on PreCompact would BLOCK compaction.\n182\t\"\"\"\n183\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n184\t\n185\timport json\n186\timport os\n187\timport sys\n188\tfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n189\tfrom pathlib import Path\n190\t\n191\tHEADER = (\n192\t    \"# Compaction log\\n\\n\"\n193\t    \"| UTC time | Session | Trigger | Focus note |\\n\"\n194\t    \"|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n195\t)\n196\t\n197\t\n198\tdef main() -> None:\n199\t    try:\n200\t        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n201\t    except Exception:\n202\t        return\n203\t    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n204\t    log = project / \"docs\" / \"process\" / \"compaction-log.md\"\n205\t    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n206\t    if not log.exists():\n207\t        log.write_text(HEADER)\n208\t    note = (event.get(\"custom_instructions\") or \"\").replace(\"|\", \"/\").replace(\"\\n\", \" \").strip()\n209\t    row = \"| {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n\".format(\n210\t        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\"),\n211\t        (event.get(\"session_id\") or \"?\")[:8],\n212\t        event.get(\"trigger\", \"unknown\"),\n213\t        note or \"(none)\",\n214\t    )\n215\t    with log.open(\"a\") as f:\n216\t        f.write(row)\n217\t\n218\t\n219\tif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n220\t    try:\n221\t        main()\n222\t    except Exception:\n223\t        pass\n224\t    sys.exit(0)\n225\t```\n226\t\n227\t**Warning:** never change its exit code to 2. On `PreCompact`, exit code 2 **blocks compaction**, which would lock you inside an overflowing session.\n228\t\n229\t## Step 6 — Confirm the hooks are registered\n230\t\n231\tThe template already registers all three in `.claude/settings.json`, together with\n232\tthe `SessionEnd` transcript saver. Read that file now so you know what is wired up:\n233\t\n234\t```bash\n235\tcat .claude/settings.json\n236\t```\n237\t\n238\t**Expected:** a `statusLine` entry plus `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `SessionEnd`\n239\thooks, each pointing at a script in `.claude/hooks/`. Check it is valid JSON:\n240\t\n241\t```bash\n242\tpython3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo \"settings OK\"\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\t**Expected:** `settings OK`. If you ever edit this file and see\n246\t`Expecting ',' delimiter`, a comma is missing at the line number shown.\n247\t\n248\t## Step 7 — Keep the state files out of git\n249\t\n250\tThe meter's scratch files are per-session and per-laptop. They must not be committed:\n251\t\n252\t```bash\n253\tgrep -qxF '.claude/state/' .gitignore || echo '.claude/state/' >> .gitignore\n254\ttail -3 .gitignore\n255\t```\n256\t\n257\t**Expected:** `.claude/state/` appears in the last lines. (`docs/process/compaction-log.md` *is* committed; it is evidence.)\n258\t\n259\t## Step 8 — Test the scripts without Claude\n260\t\n261\tPipe fake session data in, exactly as Claude Code would:\n262\t\n263\t```bash\n264\texport CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$PWD\"\n265\t\n266\techo '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"model\":{\"display_name\":\"Opus\"},\"context_window\":{\"used_percentage\":63}}' \\\n267\t  | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n268\t\n269\techo '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n270\techo '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n271\t\n272\trm -f .claude/state/ctx_demo*.json\n273\t```\n274\t\n275\t**Expected output, in order:**\n276\t\n277\t1. `[Opus] ctx 63% ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░  ⚠ compact at next green test`\n278\t2. `{\"systemMessage\": \"Context 63%: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"}`\n279\t3. *(nothing)*: the second call is silent because it already warned once.\n280\t\n281\t## Step 9 — Test it live with low thresholds\n282\t\n283\tStart Claude with thresholds so low that the first reply trips them:\n284\t\n285\t```bash\n286\tCTX_WARN_PCT=1 CTX_COMPACT_PCT=2 claude\n287\t```\n288\t\n289\t1. Look under the prompt. **Expected:** `[<model>] ctx N% ▓░░░░░░░░░`.\n290\t2. Type `/hooks`. **Expected:** `Stop` and `PreCompact` each show 1+ hooks with the source `Project Settings`. Press Esc.\n291\t3. Type `say hi`. After Claude answers, **expected:** a warning line starting `Context N%:`.\n292\t4. Type `/compact keep: hook test`. Then open `docs/process/compaction-log.md`. **Expected:** a new row ending `| manual | keep: hook test |`.\n293\t5. Type `/exit`. From now on start Claude normally (`claude`), and the real 50/60/80% thresholds apply.\n294\t\n295\tDelete the test row from `docs/process/compaction-log.md` so your log starts clean.\n296\t\n297\t## Step 10 — Commit\n298\t\n299\t```text\n300\tCommit the context-threshold hooks, settings.json, .gitignore, and tests/test_ctx_guard.py with the message \"setup: context-threshold warning hook\" and push.\n301\t```\n302\t\n303\tCheck on GitHub that the commit appears, and that `.claude/state/` is **not** in the repo.\n304\t\n305\t---\n306\t\n307\t## Using it during tickets\n308\t\n309\t| You see | Do this |\n310\t|---|---|\n311\t| Meter under 50% | Keep working. |\n312\t| `Context 5x%: … plan a /compact` | Let the current red-green cycle finish. |\n313\t| `Context 6x%: at the next green test run /compact keep: …` | As soon as the tests are green, type `/compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched` (with the real ticket number). |\n314\t| `Context 8x%: compact now …` | Compact immediately, or `/handoff` and start a new session. Afterward, ask whether the ticket should be split with `/to-tickets`. |\n315\t| A log row with trigger `auto` | The session overflowed and Claude compacted on its own. It is not an error, but the judge counts it against B6; next time, compact yourself at 60%. |\n316\t| Starting the next short ticket | `/clear`. No compaction needed. |\n317\t\n318\t## Troubleshooting\n319\t\n320\t| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n321\t|---|---|---|\n322\t| No meter under the prompt | `statusLine` block missing, or JSON invalid | Rerun the Step 6 JSON check; restart Claude |\n323\t| Meter shows `ctx --` | Your Claude Code version does not send `context_window` | Run `claude update`, restart |\n324\t| Meter works, never any warning | Stop hook not registered, or the path is wrong | `/hooks` should list it; if it shows `Failed with non-blocking status code`, the path in `settings.json` is wrong |\n325\t| `python3: command not found` inside the hook | Hook shell has a different PATH | Replace `python3` in `settings.json` with the full path from `which python3` |\n326\t| Compaction log never appears | `PreCompact` entry missing | Recheck Step 6 with `/hooks` |\n327\t| Focus note column says `(none)` | You ran `/compact` with no note, or your version names the field differently | Always type a note; if it still shows `(none)`, tell the instructor your `claude --version` |\n328\t| Warnings pop up in the wrong pane | Should not happen: each session has its own state file | Delete `.claude/state/` and restart both sessions |\n329\t\n330\tIf none of these fix it, follow the self-help ladder in the manual: reread the error, run `/hooks`, ask Claude to explain the error before changing anything, check the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [status line docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline), log it with `/teach-log`, then email the instructor with the error pasted in.\n331\t\n332\t## Saved? ✓\n333\t\n334\tBefore moving on, all of these must be true:\n335\t\n336\t- [ ] `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, `ctx_compact_log.py` committed\n337\t- [ ] `.claude/settings.json` contains `statusLine`, `Stop`, and `PreCompact` entries, and passes the JSON check\n338\t- [ ] `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` committed, and `/tdd` reported all 10 tests passing\n339\t- [ ] `.claude/state/` listed in `.gitignore` and absent from GitHub\n340\t- [ ] `claude --version` recorded in `notes/setup_check.md`\n341\t\n342\t## Complete test file (template contents)\n343\t\n344\t```python\n345\t\"\"\"Tests for the context-threshold hooks (IPHS 400 MP2, setup exercise).\"\"\"\n346\timport importlib.util\n347\timport json\n348\timport os\n349\timport subprocess\n350\timport sys\n351\tfrom pathlib import Path\n352\t\n353\tHOOKS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \".claude\" / \"hooks\"\n354\t\n355\t\n356\tdef load(name):\n357\t    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, HOOKS / f\"{name}.py\")\n358\t    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n359\t    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n360\t    return mod\n361\t\n362\t\n363\tguard = load(\"ctx_guard\")\n364\t\n365\t\n366\tdef run(script, payload, project, **env):\n367\t    return subprocess.run(\n368\t        [sys.executable, str(HOOKS / script)],\n369\t        input=json.dumps(payload),\n370\t        capture_output=True,\n371\t        text=True,\n372\t        env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(project), **env},\n373\t    )\n374\t\n375\t\n376\t# ---- pure logic -----------------------------------------------------------\n377\t\n378\tdef test_silent_below_50():\n379\t    assert guard.decide(49.9, guard.NONE) == (None, guard.NONE)\n380\t\n381\t\n382\tdef test_warns_once_at_50():\n383\t    msg, band = guard.decide(52, guard.NONE)\n384\t    assert band == guard.WARN and \"52%\" in msg\n385\t    assert guard.decide(55, band) == (None, guard.WARN)  # no nagging\n386\t\n387\t\n388\tdef test_compact_message_at_60_names_focus_note():\n389\t    msg, band = guard.decide(61, guard.WARN)\n390\t    assert band == guard.COMPACT and \"/compact keep:\" in msg\n391\t\n392\t\n393\tdef test_urgent_at_80_suggests_split():\n394\t    msg, band = guard.decide(81, guard.COMPACT)\n395\t    assert band == guard.URGENT and \"/to-tickets\" in msg\n396\t\n397\t\n398\tdef test_rearms_after_compaction():\n399\t    _, band = guard.decide(20, guard.COMPACT)   # usage dropped after /compact\n400\t    assert band == MP2 Setup Exercise — Context-Threshold Warning Hook\n\n**Course:** IPHS 400 Frontiers of AI, Kenyon College, Fall 2026 (Jon Chun)\n**Where this goes:** Student manual, Part 1 (setup), right after the template repo is cloned and `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` has run.\n**Time:** 20–30 minutes. **Token cost:** under 3% of a 5-hour window (the scripts cost nothing at runtime; hooks run outside the model).\n**Rubric link:** Factor B, item B6 \"session hygiene\" (3 pts). The judge checks that the hook works and reads `docs/process/compaction-log.md`.\n**Verified against:** Claude Code hooks and status-line docs as of 2026-09-22. Record your own version with `claude --version` in `notes/setup_check.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Why you are building this\n\nPocock's loop runs one ticket per fresh context: `/clear`, then `/implement #N`. Most tickets finish well inside one window. A long ticket does not, and a model working in a very full context forgets the ticket's acceptance criteria and starts to drift from the spec. The course rule is:\n\n- **Short ticket:** `/clear` before it. Nothing else.\n- **Long ticket:** once context passes **50–60%**, `/compact` at the next **green test** (the end of a `/tdd` red-green-refactor cycle), never in the middle of a failing test, and always with a focus note.\n\nYou cannot follow that rule if you cannot see the number. This exercise gives you a live meter and a warning that fires at the right moment.\n\n## How it works\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    CC[\"Claude Code session\"] -- \"session JSON on stdin<br/>(every refresh)\" --> SL[\"ctx_statusline.py<br/>prints: [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\"]\n    SL -- \"writes\" --> ST[\".claude/state/ctx_&lt;session&gt;.json<br/>{pct: 47.2}\"]\n    CC -- \"Stop event<br/>(end of every Claude turn)\" --> G[\"ctx_guard.py\"]\n    ST -- \"reads\" --> G\n    G -- \"first time over 50 / 60 / 80%\" --> W[\"⚠ systemMessage shown to YOU\"]\n    CC -- \"PreCompact event\" --> L[\"ctx_compact_log.py\"]\n    L -- \"appends\" --> LOG[\"docs/process/compaction-log.md<br/>(grading evidence)\"]\n```\n\nThree facts from the Claude Code docs make this design work:\n\n1. **The status line already receives the context percentage** as `context_window.used_percentage` on stdin. The status line is the customizable bar under your prompt.\n2. **A `Stop` hook fires every time Claude finishes a turn.** The end of a turn is where a natural boundary (a green test) happens, so that is when the warning should appear.\n3. **A hook's `systemMessage` is shown to the user, not to Claude.** The warning talks to you, and does not pollute Claude's context.\n\nA hook cannot type `/compact` for you. Slash commands are yours. The hook only warns; you decide.\n\nEach herdr pane or terminal tab running Claude has its own `session_id`, so parallel sessions keep separate meters and never trip each other's warnings.\n\n## The four files\n\n| File | Job | Runs when |\n|---|---|---|\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py` | Shows the meter; records the percentage | Every status-line refresh |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` | Warns at 50 / 60 / 80% | End of every Claude turn (`Stop`) |\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py` | Logs each compaction and its focus note | Before every compaction (`PreCompact`) |\n| `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` | Proves the logic works | When `/tdd` or `/code-review` runs the suite |\n\n---\n\n## Step 1 — Check Python\n\nIn Ghostty (macOS) or Windows Terminal (WSL2), inside your `iphs400-mp2-cms` folder:\n\n```bash\npython3 --version\n```\n\n**Expected:** `Python 3.9` or newer (the `uv` setup from the setup manual gives you 3.12).\n**If you see `command not found`:** macOS runs `xcode-select --install`; WSL2 runs `sudo apt install -y python3`. Then retry.\n\n## Step 2 — Open the hook files\n\nThe template already contains all four files. Open the folder in VS Code:\n\n```bash\ncode .\n```\n\nIn the Explorer panel, expand `.claude/hooks/`. You should see `ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, and `ctx_compact_log.py`.\n\n**If `.claude` is not visible:** VS Code hides nothing by default, but macOS Finder hides dot-folders. Use VS Code, or run `ls -la .claude/hooks` in the terminal.\n\n## Step 3 — Read the status-line script\n\nThis file is complete. Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\n\nClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\nJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\n  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\n  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\n     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\nIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\n    ws = data.get(\"workspace\") or {}\n    return Path(\n        os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\n        or ws.get(\"project_dir\")\n        or ws.get(\"current_dir\")\n        or os.getcwd()\n    )\n\n\ndef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\n    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\n    return \"▓\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        print(\"ctx ?\")\n        return\n\n    model = (data.get(\"model\") or {}).get(\"display_name\", \"Claude\")\n    pct = (data.get(\"context_window\") or {}).get(\"used_percentage\")\n    if pct is None:\n        print(f\"[{model}] ctx --\")\n        return\n    pct = float(pct)\n\n    session = data.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    try:\n        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        tmp = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\"\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\"pct\": pct, \"ts\": time.time()}))\n        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\")  # atomic swap\n    except OSError:\n        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\n\n    flag = \"  ⚠ compact at next green test\" if pct >= 60 else \"\"\n    print(f\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\n\nThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Seven of the ten tests in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` fail until you finish it. This is your first practice run of the loop on something tiny.\n\nIn a fresh Claude Code session:\n\n```text\n/clear\n/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests or any other function.\n```\n\n`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. You do not type `pytest` yourself.\n\nThe rules `decide()` must follow:\n\n- Map the percentage to a band: 0 = below 50, 1 = 50+, 2 = 60+, 3 = 80+ (the thresholds come from `thresholds()`).\n- **Warn once per upward crossing.** Going from 52% to 55% must stay quiet.\n- **Re-arm after compaction.** When usage drops (after `/compact` or `/clear`), remember the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n\nWhen the tests pass, compare your version with the complete file below.\n\n\n## Step 5 — Read the compaction logger\n\nThis file is complete. It writes the evidence the judge reads for rubric item B6.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"PreCompact hook: log every compaction to docs/process/compaction-log.md.\n\nThis is grading evidence for rubric item B6 (session hygiene):\n  - trigger \"manual\" + a focus note  = you compacted on purpose (good)\n  - trigger \"auto\"                   = the session overflowed (fix the habit)\nNever exits 2: exit 2 on PreCompact would BLOCK compaction.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHEADER = (\n    \"# Compaction log\\n\\n\"\n    \"| UTC time | Session | Trigger | Focus note |\\n\"\n    \"|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    log = project / \"docs\" / \"process\" / \"compaction-log.md\"\n    log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    if not log.exists():\n        log.write_text(HEADER)\n    note = (event.get(\"custom_instructions\") or \"\").replace(\"|\", \"/\").replace(\"\\n\", \" \").strip()\n    row = \"| {} | {} | {} | {} |\\n\".format(\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\"),\n        (event.get(\"session_id\") or \"?\")[:8],\n        event.get(\"trigger\", \"unknown\"),\n        note or \"(none)\",\n    )\n    with log.open(\"a\") as f:\n        f.write(row)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    sys.exit(0)\n```\n\n**Warning:** never change its exit code to 2. On `PreCompact`, exit code 2 **blocks compaction**, which would lock you inside an overflowing session.\n\n## Step 6 — Confirm the hooks are registered\n\nThe template already registers all three in `.claude/settings.json`, together with\nthe `SessionEnd` transcript saver. Read that file now so you know what is wired up:\n\n```bash\ncat .claude/settings.json\n```\n\n**Expected:** a `statusLine` entry plus `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `SessionEnd`\nhooks, each pointing at a script in `.claude/hooks/`. Check it is valid JSON:\n\n```bash\npython3 -m json.tool .claude/settings.json > /dev/null && echo \"settings OK\"\n```\n\n**Expected:** `settings OK`. If you ever edit this file and see\n`Expecting ',' delimiter`, a comma is missing at the line number shown.\n\n## Step 7 — Keep the state files out of git\n\nThe meter's scratch files are per-session and per-laptop. They must not be committed:\n\n```bash\ngrep -qxF '.claude/state/' .gitignore || echo '.claude/state/' >> .gitignore\ntail -3 .gitignore\n```\n\n**Expected:** `.claude/state/` appears in the last lines. (`docs/process/compaction-log.md` *is* committed; it is evidence.)\n\n## Step 8 — Test the scripts without Claude\n\nPipe fake session data in, exactly as Claude Code would:\n\n```bash\nexport CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$PWD\"\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"model\":{\"display_name\":\"Opus\"},\"context_window\":{\"used_percentage\":63}}' \\\n  | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\necho '{\"session_id\":\"demo\",\"hook_event_name\":\"Stop\"}' | python3 .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n\nrm -f .claude/state/ctx_demo*.json\n```\n\n**Expected output, in order:**\n\n1. `[Opus] ctx 63% ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░  ⚠ compact at next green test`\n2. `{\"systemMessage\": \"Context 63%: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"}`\n3. *(nothing)*: the second call is silent because it already warned once.\n\n## Step 9 — Test it live with low thresholds\n\nStart Claude with thresholds so low that the first reply trips them:\n\n```bash\nCTX_WARN_PCT=1 CTX_COMPACT_PCT=2 claude\n```\n\n1. Look under the prompt. **Expected:** `[<model>] ctx N% ▓░░░░░░░░░`.\n2. Type `/hooks`. **Expected:** `Stop` and `PreCompact` each show 1+ hooks with the source `Project Settings`. Press Esc.\n3. Type `say hi`. After Claude answers, **expected:** a warning line starting `Context N%:`.\n4. Type `/compact keep: hook test`. Then open `docs/process/compaction-log.md`. **Expected:** a new row ending `| manual | keep: hook test |`.\n5. Type `/exit`. From now on start Claude normally (`claude`), and the real 50/60/80% thresholds apply.\n\nDelete the test row from `docs/process/compaction-log.md` so your log starts clean.\n\n## Step 10 — Commit\n\n```text\nCommit the context-threshold hooks, settings.json, .gitignore, and tests/test_ctx_guard.py with the message \"setup: context-threshold warning hook\" and push.\n```\n\nCheck on GitHub that the commit appears, and that `.claude/state/` is **not** in the repo.\n\n---\n\n## Using it during tickets\n\n| You see | Do this |\n|---|---|\n| Meter under 50% | Keep working. |\n| `Context 5x%: … plan a /compact` | Let the current red-green cycle finish. |\n| `Context 6x%: at the next green test run /compact keep: …` | As soon as the tests are green, type `/compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched` (with the real ticket number). |\n| `Context 8x%: compact now …` | Compact immediately, or `/handoff` and start a new session. Afterward, ask whether the ticket should be split with `/to-tickets`. |\n| A log row with trigger `auto` | The session overflowed and Claude compacted on its own. It is not an error, but the judge counts it against B6; next time, compact yourself at 60%. |\n| Starting the next short ticket | `/clear`. No compaction needed. |\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| No meter under the prompt | `statusLine` block missing, or JSON invalid | Rerun the Step 6 JSON check; restart Claude |\n| Meter shows `ctx --` | Your Claude Code version does not send `context_window` | Run `claude update`, restart |\n| Meter works, never any warning | Stop hook not registered, or the path is wrong | `/hooks` should list it; if it shows `Failed with non-blocking status code`, the path in `settings.json` is wrong |\n| `python3: command not found` inside the hook | Hook shell has a different PATH | Replace `python3` in `settings.json` with the full path from `which python3` |\n| Compaction log never appears | `PreCompact` entry missing | Recheck Step 6 with `/hooks` |\n| Focus note column says `(none)` | You ran `/compact` with no note, or your version names the field differently | Always type a note; if it still shows `(none)`, tell the instructor your `claude --version` |\n| Warnings pop up in the wrong pane | Should not happen: each session has its own state file | Delete `.claude/state/` and restart both sessions |\n\nIf none of these fix it, follow the self-help ladder in the manual: reread the error, run `/hooks`, ask Claude to explain the error before changing anything, check the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [status line docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline), log it with `/teach-log`, then email the instructor with the error pasted in.\n\n## Saved? ✓\n\nBefore moving on, all of these must be true:\n\n- [ ] `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, `ctx_compact_log.py` committed\n- [ ] `.claude/settings.json` contains `statusLine`, `Stop`, and `PreCompact` entries, and passes the JSON check\n- [ ] `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` committed, and `/tdd` reported all 10 tests passing\n- [ ] `.claude/state/` listed in `.gitignore` and absent from GitHub\n- [ ] `claude --version` recorded in `notes/setup_check.md`\n\n## Complete test file (template contents)\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Tests for the context-threshold hooks (IPHS 400 MP2, setup exercise).\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport json\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHOOKS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \".claude\" / \"hooks\"\n\n\ndef load(name):\n    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, HOOKS / f\"{name}.py\")\n    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)\n    return mod\n\n\nguard = load(\"ctx_guard\")\n\n\ndef run(script, payload, project, **env):\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(HOOKS / script)],\n        input=json.dumps(payload),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(project), **env},\n    )\n\n\n# ---- pure logic -----------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_silent_below_50():\n    assert guard.decide(49.9, guard.NONE) == (None, guard.NONE)\n\n\ndef test_warns_once_at_50():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(52, guard.NONE)\n    assert band == guard.WARN and \"52%\" in msg\n    assert guard.decide(55, band) == (None, guard.WARN)  # no nagging\n\n\ndef test_compact_message_at_60_names_focus_note():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(61, guard.WARN)\n    assert band == guard.COMPACT and \"/compact keep:\" in msg\n\n\ndef test_urgent_at_80_suggests_split():\n    msg, band = guard.decide(81, guard.COMPACT)\n    assert band == guard.URGENT and \"/to-tickets\" in msg\n\n\ndef test_rearms_after_compaction():\n    _, band = guard.decide(20, guard.COMPACT)   # usage dropped after /compact\n    assert band == guard.NONE\n    msg, _ = guard.decide(51, band)             # next crossing warns again\n    assert msg is not None\n\n\ndef test_thresholds_from_env(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", \"1\")\n    msg, _ = guard.decide(2, guard.NONE)\n    assert msg is not None\n\n\n# ---- end to end: status line -> Stop hook ---------------------------------\n\ndef test_statusline_then_stop_hook(tmp_path):\n    sl = run(\"ctx_statusline.py\",\n             {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"model\": {\"display_name\": \"Opus\"},\n              \"context_window\": {\"used_percentage\": 63.4}}, tmp_path)\n    assert \"ctx 63%\" in sl.stdout\n    out = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"hook_event_name\": \"Stop\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert out.returncode == 0\n    assert \"/compact\" in json.loads(out.stdout)[\"systemMessage\"]\n    again = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"s1\", \"hook_event_name\": \"Stop\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert again.stdout.strip() == \"\"           # warned once, then quiet\n\n\ndef test_stop_hook_silent_without_data(tmp_path):\n    out = run(\"ctx_guard.py\", {\"session_id\": \"nobody\"}, tmp_path)\n    assert out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_stop_hook_survives_garbage_stdin(tmp_path):\n    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HOOKS / \"ctx_guard.py\")],\n                         input=\"not json\", capture_output=True, text=True,\n                         env={**os.environ, \"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\": str(tmp_path)})\n    assert out.returncode == 0\n\n\ndef test_precompact_logs_focus_note(tmp_path):\n    run(\"ctx_compact_log.py\",\n        {\"session_id\": \"abcdef123\", \"trigger\": \"manual\",\n         \"custom_instructions\": \"keep: ticket #5 criteria\"}, tmp_path)\n    log = (tmp_path / \"docs/process/compaction-log.md\").read_text()\n    assert \"| manual | {"parentUuid":"f41356eb-57d3-4480-a742-4148591c2b5b","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"852c5e2c-9582-4744-b0f3-4fd6296fbf54","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/sphod/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. The hook never blocks and never\nruns /compact itself: slash commands are yours to type.\n\nThresholds (override when launching:  CTX_WARN_PCT=1 claude  to test):\n  CTX_WARN_PCT     default 50  -> \"plan a /compact\"\n  CTX_COMPACT_PCT  default 60  -> \"/compact at the next green test\"\n  urgent = CTX_COMPACT_PCT + 20 -> \"compact or /handoff now; consider splitting\"\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNONE, WARN, COMPACT, URGENT = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\n\ndef thresholds() -> tuple[float, float, float]:\n    warn = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_WARN_PCT\", 50))\n    compact = float(os.environ.get(\"CTX_COMPACT_PCT\", 60))\n    return warn, compact, compact + 20\n\n\ndef band_for(pct: float, warn: float, compact: float, urgent: float) -> int:\n    if pct >= urgent:\n        return URGENT\n    if pct >= compact:\n        return COMPACT\n    if pct >= warn:\n        return WARN\n    return NONE\n\n\ndef message_for(band: int, pct: float) -> str:\n    p = f\"{pct:.0f}%\"\n    return {\n        WARN: (\n            f\"Context {p}: finish the current red-green cycle, then plan a \"\n            \"/compact at the next green test.\"\n        ),\n        COMPACT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: at the next green test run  /compact keep: ticket #N \"\n            \"acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\"\n        ),\n        URGENT: (\n            f\"Context {p}: compact now (or /handoff and start fresh). If this \"\n            \"ticket keeps overflowing, split it with /to-tickets.\"\n        ),\n    }[band]\n\n\ndef decide(pct: float, last_band: int) -> tuple[str | None, int]:\n    \"\"\"Pure function (unit-tested): return (message or None, band to store).\n\n    Warn once per upward crossing. When usage drops (after /compact or\n    /clear), store the lower band so the next crossing warns again.\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise A: implement me with /tdd\")\n\nLEDGER_COLUMNS = [\n    \"ts\", \"session\", \"phase\", \"provider\", \"model\", \"effort\",\n    \"ctx_pct\", \"five_h_pct\", \"weekly_pct\",\n]\n\n\ndef log_usage(project: Path, session: str, state: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one row per turn to notes/usage-ledger.csv (rubric item B7).\"\"\"\n    ledger = project / \"notes\" / \"usage-ledger.csv\"\n    phase_file = project / \".claude\" / \"state\" / \"phase\"\n    try:\n        phase = phase_file.read_text().strip() or \"unlabelled\"\n    except OSError:\n        phase = \"unlabelled\"\n\n    def cell(value: object) -> str:\n        return \"\" if value is None else str(value)\n\n    row = [\n        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"),\n        session[:8], phase, cell(state.get(\"provider\")), cell(state.get(\"model\")),\n        cell(state.get(\"effort\")), f\"{float(state.get('pct', 0)):.1f}\",\n        cell(state.get(\"five_h\")), cell(state.get(\"weekly\")),\n    ]\n    try:\n        ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        new = not ledger.exists()\n        with ledger.open(\"a\", newline=\"\") as f:\n            writer = csv.writer(f)\n            if new:\n                writer.writerow(LEDGER_COLUMNS)\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    try:\n        event = json.load(sys.stdin)\n    except Exception:\n        return\n    project = Path(os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\") or event.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n    session = event.get(\"session_id\") or \"default\"\n    state_dir = project / \".claude\" / \"state\"\n    ctx_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}.json\"\n    band_file = state_dir / f\"ctx_{session}_band.json\"\n\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(ctx_file.read_text())\n        pct = float(state[\"pct\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        return  # no status-line data yet: stay silent\n    try:\n        last_band = int(json.loads(band_file.read_text())[\"band\"])\n    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        last_band = NONE\n\n    log_usage(project, session, state)\n\n    msg, band = decide(pct, last_band)\n    try:\n        band_file.write_text(json.dumps({\"band\": band}))\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n    if msg:\n        print(json.dumps({\"systemMessage\": msg}))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    try:\n        main()\n    except Exception:\n        pass  # a warning hook must never break the session\n I read the `spend()` stub in `scripts/usage_report.py` and the tests in `tests/test_usage_report.py`.\n\n**What `spend()` has to do**\nIt takes the readings of one usage meter, in order, and returns how much the meter rose in total.\n- **Rises add up:** `[10, 12, 15]` gives 5.\n- **A drop is a reset, not negative spending:** `[80, 5, 9]` gives 4. The 80→5 drop adds nothing, and the new baseline is 5, so only the rise from 5 to 9 counts.\n- **Blanks are skipped:** `[None, 4, None, 7]` gives 3. A blank doesn't reset the baseline, so 4→7 counts as a rise.\n- **Empty or all-blank lists give 0.0.**\n\nThe way to do it is to keep the previous non-blank reading, and for each new reading add `current - previous` only when it's positive. It needs about 6 lines, and I wouldn't change anything else in the file.\n\n**Which tests cover it**\n- **Four direct tests** call `spend()` for rises, resets, blanks and empty input.\n- **Three report tests** run the whole script. They check:\n  - phase grouping, which depends on `spend()`;\n  - that the over-budget forecast prints the right fix list;\n  - that a backup provider like `@api.z.ai` shows in the output.\n- **`test_missing_ledger_explains`** doesn't call `spend()` and should already pass.\n\n**One limitation:** after a reset, any spending between the reset and the first new reading is lost. That undercounts slightly. The design accepts it, and the exercise says \"ignore resets\", so I'm not going to change it.\n\nI don't expect to touch anything except the one function body. {"parentUuid":"6fefb299-37a9-4702-b519-e281f1279303","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"effc7cfd-4efb-4695-8c0c-4193dbfff470","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01VWpWYRpvLyMh2smABReSJY","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /home/sphod/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/scripts/usage_report.py has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"e8fc8085-a1ab-4963-8da7-90a37ea5ce41","timestamp":"2026-10-02T14:52:51.113Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/sphod/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/scripts/usage_report.py","oldString":"    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise B: implement me with /tdd\")\n","newString":"    total, previous = 0.0, None\n    for value in series:\n        if value is None:\n            continue\n        if previous is not None and value > previous:\n            total += value - previous\n        previous = value\n    return total\n","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Turn notes/usage-ledger.csv into a plan-vs-actual budget report.\n\nUsage:\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py                 # summary + forecast\n    uv run python scripts/usage_report.py --remaining 4   # 4 tickets still to do\n\nWhy positive deltas: the 5-hour and weekly meters RESET (drop to 0) when their\nwindow rolls over, and the weekly one only ever climbs inside a week. Summing\nonly the increases between consecutive rows measures what you actually spent\nand ignores the resets. That is what spend() does, and it is your exercise.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nLEDGER = Path(\"notes/usage-ledger.csv\")\n\n\ndef spend(series: list[float | None]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Total rise across a meter that can reset to a lower value.\n\n    Sum every increase between consecutive readings; ignore blanks (None) and\n    any drop, which means the window reset.\n\n    >>> spend([10.0, 12.0, 15.0])\n    5.0\n    >>> spend([80.0, 5.0, 9.0])\n    4.0\n    >>> spend([None, 4.0, None, 7.0])\n    3.0\n    \"\"\"\n    raise NotImplementedError(\"MP2 Exercise B: implement me with /tdd\")\n\ndef read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    with path.open(newline=\"\") as f:\n        return list(csv.DictReader(f))\n\n\ndef to_float(text: str | None) -> float | None:\n    try:\n        return float(text) if text not in (None, \"\") else None\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\ndef by_phase(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    phases: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(\n        lambda: {\"turns\": 0, \"five\": [], \"weekly\": [], \"models\": set(), \"providers\": set()}\n    )\n    for row in rows:\n        phase = phases[row.get(\"phase\") or \"unlabelled\"]\n        phase[\"turns\"] += 1\n        phase[\"five\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"five_h_pct\")))\n        phase[\"weekly\"].append(to_float(row.get(\"weekly_pct\")))\n        if row.get(\"model\"):\n            phase[\"models\"].add(row[\"model\"])\n        if row.get(\"provider\"):\n            phase[\"providers\"].add(row[\"provider\"])\n    return phases\n\n\ndef ticket_phases(phases: dict[str, dict]) -> list[str]:\n    return sorted(p for p in phases if p.upper().startswith(\"T\") and p[1:].isdigit())\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--ledger\", type=Path, default=LEDGER)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--remaining\", type=int, default=0, help=\"tickets not yet built\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if not args.ledger.exists():\n        raise SystemExit(f\"No ledger at {args.ledger}. Is the Stop hook registered?\")\n    rows = read_rows(args.ledger)\n    if not rows:\n        raise SystemExit(\"Ledger is empty.\")\n    phases = by_phase(rows)\n\n    print(f\"{'phase':<14}{'turns':>6}{'5h spent':>10}{'weekly':>9}  models / provider\")\n    for name, data in sorted(phases.items()):\n        mix = \",\".join(sorted(data[\"models\"])) or \"?\"\n        prov = \",\".join(sorted(data[\"providers\"] - {\"anthropic\"}))\n        print(f\"{name:<14}{data['turns']:>6}{spend(data['five']):>9.1f}%\"\n              f\"{spend(data['weekly']):>8.1f}%  {mix}{(' @' + prov) if prov else ''}\")\n\n    tickets = ticket_phases(phases)\n    if tickets:\n        per = sum(spend(phases[t][\"weekly\"]) for t in tickets) / len(tickets)\n        print(f\"\\nTickets done: {len(tickets)} · average weekly cost per ticket: {per:.1f}%\")\n        last = next((to_float(r.get(\"weekly_pct\")) for r in reversed(rows)\n                     if to_float(r.get(\"weekly_pct\")) is not None), None)\n        if last is not None and args.remaining:\n            need, headroom = per * args.remaining, 100 - last\n            verdict = \"FITS\" if need <= headroom * 0.8 else \"TIGHT\" if need <= headroom else \"OVER BUDGET\"\n            print(f\"Forecast: {args.remaining} tickets need ~{need:.0f}% of the weekly cap; \"\n                  f\"{headroom:.0f}% remains → {verdict}\")\n            if verdict != \"FITS\":\n                print(\"Fix in this order: 1) lower effort  2) switch to Sonnet/Haiku  \"\n                      \"3) /clear more often  4) split fat tickets  5) Plan B backend (declare it)\")\n    else:\n        print(\"\\nNo ticket phases yet.
